parcel_summary.address: 2165 Sandy Pines Dr NE, Palm Bay FL 32905

constraints.name: FEMA Zone A Flood (SFHA)
constraints.description: Entire parcel within Special Flood Hazard Area. No Base Flood Elevation determined (Study Type: NP — approximate Zone A).
constraints.regulatory_basis: 44 CFR Part 60, Florida Building Code 8th Edition, Palm Bay Code Chapter 174
development_impact: BFE must be established via hydraulic study (HEC-RAS modeling) before ANY building permit
All habitable floors must be elevated above BFE + 1 ft freeboard (FBC requirement)
Floodplain Development Permit required from City of Palm Bay
Elevation Certificate (FEMA FF-206-FY-22-152) required at foundation, pre-drywall, and final inspection
Flood insurance mandatory for federally-backed mortgages
15-30% construction cost premium for elevated foundation systems
Residential floodproofing NOT permitted under NFIP — must elevate
mitigation_options: LOMA/LOMR-F: If fill raises lot above BFE, parcel can be removed from SFHA (no FEMA fee, ~60-day processing)
Elevated construction: Pile/column foundation or fill pad to achieve required elevation
Flood-resistant materials required below BFE per FEMA Technical Bulletin 2 (FIA-TB-2)

constraints.name: NWI Wetland PEM1Cd (Freshwater Emergent)
constraints.description: Entire 1.114-acre parcel sits within a 10.316-acre NWI-mapped freshwater emergent wetland polygon. Classification: Palustrine, Emergent, Persistent, Seasonally Flooded, Partially Drained/Ditched.
constraints.regulatory_basis: Clean Water Act Section 404 (FL assumed jurisdiction), Florida ERP rules 62-330 FAC, SJRWMD 40C-4/40C-40/40C-42
development_impact: Professional wetland delineation required to determine jurisdictional boundary
25-ft wetland buffer setback likely required by SJRWMD
Section 404 permit (via FDEP state-assumed program) if any wetland fill proposed
Avoidance/minimization/mitigation sequence must be demonstrated
Mitigation required for any unavoidable wetland impact — purchase of mitigation bank credits
Partially drained (d) modifier may reduce mitigation requirements but does not eliminate them
mitigation_options: Mitigation bank credits: Farmton Mitigation Bank is the primary bank for south Brevard
Credit cost: $125,000-$200,000 per UMAM credit in this service area
Estimated credits needed: 0.3-0.5 UMAM credits (depending on impact area and functional assessment)
On-site preservation/enhancement possible for remaining wetland areas

constraints.name: Wellhead Protection Easement
constraints.description: 200-ft radius circular easement around City of Palm Bay public water supply well. Covers western 47% of parcel.
constraints.regulatory_basis: Florida DEP Chapter 62-521 FAC — Wellhead Protection Areas
development_impact: No new construction within 200-ft radius
No new impervious surfaces (may allow pervious pavement — requires city approval)
No regulated substance storage
No septic systems within wellhead protection zone
Surface parking and open space/recreation may be permitted (survey annotates 'PARKING' in this zone)

resolution.source: Tim Roberts, Palm Bay Utilities, Sept 11, 2025
resolution.mechanism: Well decommissioning when alternative supply sources are developed
resolution.phase_2_opportunity: After easement vacated, additional 0.524 acres becomes buildable

constraints.name: HOA CC&Rs — Multifamily Likely Prohibited
constraints.description: Sandy Pines Preserve is a gated HOA community of exclusively 1-2 story single-family homes and townhomes. CC&Rs (OR Book 3636, Page 2327) almost certainly prohibit 3-4 story multifamily construction.
evidence: All existing structures are 1-2 story SF/townhome across all phases
HOA incorporated under FL Chapter 720 (Homeowners Association Act)
No apartments/condos/multifamily exist anywhere in community
Typical late-1990s gated community CC&Rs restrict use to single-family/townhome
3 separate HOA entities govern the community
resolution_options: Obtain and review actual CC&Rs (OR Book 3636/2327)
CC&R amendment: typically requires 75% supermajority HOA vote (extremely unlikely)
Legal separation: attempt to remove parcel from HOA jurisdiction (requires attorney analysis)
Alternative use: develop consistent with CC&Rs (single-family/townhome)

constraints.name: No Sewer or Water Service Available
constraints.description: Palm Bay GIS SWANC_Not_Impacted layer confirms Sewer_Avail=NO, Water_Avail=NO. Parcel not in any SANC/WANC phase. Septic infeasible near wellhead in flood zone.
constraints.source: Palm Bay GIS — SWANC_Not_Impacted/MapServer/0, queried Feb 6, 2026
constraints.neighbor_context: Adjacent parcels (2153, 2240, 2260, 2300 Sandy Pines Dr) DO have water and sewer available, suggesting main may be nearby but not extended to this parcel's frontage.
development_impact: Sewer main extension required at developer cost
Water main extension may be required despite proximity of wellhead
Estimated sewer extension: $50-$100/linear foot
Distance to nearest sewer main: unknown (likely at 2153 Sandy Pines Dr, adjacent parcel)

triggers: Project disturbs >1 acre (parcel = 1.114 acres — triggers ERP)
Work within 100-year flood zone (entire parcel in Zone A)
sjrwmd_erp_requirements.permit_category: Standard General ERP (project <640 acres, <50 ac wetland impact)
sjrwmd_erp_requirements.review_timeline_days: 60-90 (standard general), up to 180 with RAI (Request for Additional Information)

pre_application_conference.purpose: Discuss wetland delineation results, stormwater design, and mitigation strategy before formal application

required_submittals: Site plan showing existing and proposed conditions
Stormwater management calculations (25-year/24-hour design storm per MTWCD)
Professional wetland delineation report with survey
Wetland impact assessment and mitigation plan
Hydraulic analysis establishing BFE (if not available from FEMA)

palm_bay_hcp.scrub_jay_fee: $125 per quarter-acre ($560 for 1.114 acres) — paid with building permit
palm_bay_hcp.nesting_season_restriction: March 1 - June 30 — land clearing PROHIBITED in occupied scrub-jay polygons

gopher_tortoise.survey_required: 100% survey of all upland areas before any land clearing
gopher_tortoise.relocation_permit: FWC relocation permit required if burrows found

wood_stork.consultation: USFWS consultation may be required if parcel within 18.6-mile Core Foraging Area of active colony
wood_stork.habitat_relevance: PEM1Cd wetland is suitable foraging habitat

bald_eagle.check_required: FWC eagle nest locator — 660-ft buffer from active nests

items.item: Flood study / BFE determination (HEC-RAS hydraulic modeling)
Listed species surveys (gopher tortoise, scrub-jay, wood stork)
Environmental consultant package (ERP application, mitigation plan, water quality)
Palm Bay HCP scrub-jay fee (4.5 quarter-acres)

estimated_environmental_costs.largest_item: Wetland mitigation credits ($40K-$100K) — 52% of low-end / 49% of high-end

comparison_to_land_value.assessment: Environmental costs at minimum ($77K) are 1.4x the land value ($55K). At maximum ($203K), they are 3.7x the land value. This severely compromises project economics.

constraint_interaction_analysis.flood_plus_wetland: Zone A flood zone and PEM1Cd wetland are likely co-occurring on much of the parcel. Seasonally flooded wetland is consistent with SFHA designation. This overlap may simplify some permitting (joint ERP/floodplain review) but increases mitigation costs.
constraint_interaction_analysis.wellhead_plus_flood: Wellhead easement zone (47% of parcel) is also in Zone A. No construction allowed in wellhead zone regardless of flood status. Parking/open space in this zone still requires flood-compatible design.
constraint_interaction_analysis.wellhead_plus_wetland: Wellhead easement zone may contain jurisdictional wetlands. If so, even parking may require wetland impact assessment.
constraint_interaction_analysis.hoa_plus_all: Even if all environmental constraints are resolved (at $77K-$203K cost), HOA CC&Rs may still prohibit the intended use. CC&R review must precede any environmental spending.
constraint_interaction_analysis.sewer_plus_wellhead: Septic is infeasible within wellhead protection zone. Sewer extension required. If sewer main is at adjacent parcel (2153), extension cost may be manageable ($5K-$15K).

recommended_sequence.gate: FATAL — if multifamily prohibited and cannot be amended, project is not viable for intended use

Determines actual jurisdictional wetland boundary on parcel
Determines required building elevation and construction cost premium

recommended_sequence.action: Listed species surveys (gopher tortoise, scrub-jay check)
recommended_sequence.gate: Must be completed before any land clearing
Staff guidance on mitigation strategy and stormwater design

recommended_sequence.action: Formal ERP application with mitigation plan
